prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 manifesto, “A Future Fair for All,” sets a post-crisis plan built on four pillars: rebuild the economy, protect and reform public services, strengthen society, and renew politics.

Economy and public finances
- Secure the recovery with no in-year cuts; more than halve the deficit in four years via growth, fair taxes and efficiencies, while protecting frontline childcare, schools, the NHS and policing.
- Fair tax measures include a 50p rate over £150k, reduced pension tax relief for the best-off, and a 1p NI rise (excluding earners under £20k and pensioners); VAT on essentials not extended.
- £20bn+ efficiency savings, public-sector pay cap (1% for 2011–13), pension reforms, asset sales; protect mortgage rates through monetary stability.

Banking, business and jobs
- Sweeping banking reform (higher capital, “living wills,” bonus discipline, global levy), more competition and mutuals; realise taxpayer stakes for best return.
- UK Finance for Growth (£4bn) plus Growth Capital and Innovation funds; R&D tax credits, patent box, stronger capital allowances.
- Industrial strategy: Green Investment Bank, low‑carbon and high‑tech focus; infrastructure: High Speed Rail, electrification, Crossrail, universal broadband (funded by a phone-line levy), EV charging rollout; Heathrow third runway with strict conditions.
- Company reform: stronger stewardship, transparency in takeovers, two‑thirds shareholder threshold; promote employee/mutual ownership.
- Jobs/welfare: Future Jobs Fund (200k jobs), guarantee work after two years’ unemployment (mandatory), tougher incapacity reassessments with support; Minimum Wage to rise at least with earnings; “Better Off in Work” £40/wk; apprenticeships and Skills Accounts; small business support, rate relief; People’s Bank at Post Office, universal access to basic bank accounts, clampdown on high‑cost credit.

Housing and living standards
- Stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% rate over £1m); build more affordable/social homes; tougher landlord standards and repossession protection; expand savings via ISAs, Savings Gateway, Child Trust Fund.

Education
- Increase frontline spend on Sure Start, free childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places.
- 3Rs guarantee with one‑to‑one/small‑group tuition; personal tutors; stronger action on failing schools via accredited groups/mergers; fair admissions and a local pupil premium.
- More science, languages, Diplomas; extend school day childcare; expand advanced apprenticeships; HE funding review with widened access.

Health and care
- Legal patient guarantees: treatment within 18 weeks or funded private care; cancer test results within one week; NHS health checks for 40–74s; free choice of any qualified provider; evening/weekend GP access; expand mental health IAPT; more home-based care and one‑to‑one cancer nursing.
- Deliver up to £20bn NHS efficiencies, reinvested; no top‑down NHS reorganisation.
- National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for greatest needs; from 2014 cap residential care costs after two years; expand individual budgets.

Safety, immigration and communities
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing with local accountability; early intervention for 50k problem families; faster, tougher ASB action with a right to injunctions; expand Community Payback; use CCTV/DNA with safeguards.
- Immigration: Australian‑style points system, no unskilled migration from outside EU, stronger English and citizenship requirements; Migration Impact Fund.

Families, pensions and work
- “Father’s Month” of paid leave; Toddler Tax Credit; extend flexible working (end default retirement at 65).
- Restore earnings link for the Basic State Pension from 2012; auto‑enrolment and Personal Pension Accounts.

Environment and rural
- About 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; renewables, new nuclear, CCS; home insulation via “Pay As You Save,” smart meters; towards zero waste with landfill bans; protect Green Belt, expand habitats/forests; Supermarket Ombudsman; rural services and broadband.

Culture and civil society
- 2012 Olympics legacy; supporter trusts in football; free museums; protect post offices/pubs; back social enterprise/mutuals; open data and digital government.

Political and constitutional reform
- Referendums on Alternative Vote and an elected Second Chamber (staged); fixed‑term Parliaments; lobbyist register; ban MPs’ lobbying jobs; free vote on votes at 16 after improved citizenship education; stronger local government, city‑region powers; further devolution (Scotland/Wales).

Global role and defence
- Afghanistan strategy focused on protecting people, training Afghan forces, and political settlement; support troops and veterans; Strategic Defence Review; maintain independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Lead in an outward‑facing EU; meet 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; drive MDGs; reform UN/IFIs/G20/NATO; tackle climate change, security and development together.
